meta.experiment: Skill-transfer test (stage 1: N=5/arm) on two_arm_lift — validate ASPIRE layer 2
meta.question: Does seeding a lift run's library with HANDOVER-provenance skills beat an empty library? (i.e. do learned skills transfer across tasks?)
meta.design: Two arms, single manipulated variable = library contents. S = seeded with 2 handover-provenance skills (lift-provenance excluded); E = empty. Both: opus repair, s_dbg [0,1,2], s_val 100-119 held-out, theta 1.0, debug_rounds 2, evosearch OFF (t=0), pristine baseline md5 0ada19ef, isolated dirs.
meta.run_status: COMPLETE, clean — 10/10 runs, no credit/crash failures, no tainted runs.

mechanism_verified_live.arm_S_skills_injected: All 5 S reps: skills.md contained BOTH handover skills (allocate-shared-object-span-between-two-effectors, keyframe-geometry-from-trace-images). The seed reached the repair actor every time.
mechanism_verified_live.conclusion: This is a genuine result, not an inert run — the transfer channel fired; the skills simply did not help.

test.statistic: Mann-Whitney U (S vs E), one-sided, tie-corrected normal approx
test.note: z<0 => the SEEDED arm ranks LOWER. One-sided p for S>E is ~0.83 (direction is against the hypothesis). One-sided p for the observed E>S direction is ~0.17 — also not significant.

verdict.headline: NO evidence that seeding handover-provenance skills improves lift repair. Every summary statistic favors the EMPTY arm: mean 0.44 (S) vs 0.63 (E), median 0.35 vs 0.75, P(val>=0.80) 0.20 vs 0.40. The point estimate is a (non-significant) NEGATIVE transfer.
verdict.significance: Not significant either way (U=8, z=-0.946; |z| p~0.17) — same high-variance regime as the ablation. We reject H1 (skills help) in direction and cannot claim a benefit; we also cannot claim a significant harm.
verdict.honest_conclusion: On this task pair, ASPIRE's skill layer does NOT demonstrably transfer — a legitimate, important negative for layer 2. The transfer mechanism fired (skills reached the actor in all 5 S reps), so this is not a plumbing failure.
verdict.plausible_explanation: Both arms independently ADMITTED grasp-orientation skills during their own runs (S and E winners both discovered perception-aligned/yaw-aligned top-down grasps). The repair actor re-derives the needed geometry from THIS run's traces regardless of the seed, so pre-seeded cross-task skills add little the actor could not already obtain. Consistent with the traces-ablation finding that traces carry most of the repair signal.

recommended_next.primary: Do NOT chase significance by brute N (same variance wall as the ablation; a negative/null point estimate is unlikely to flip to a positive significant result). Report this honest negative.
recommended_next.if_pursued: A fairer positive-control would seed the strongest lift-relevant skill and pick a target task whose baseline the actor CANNOT solve from its own traces (so the skill supplies genuinely missing info). Also: paired seeds to cut variance. Both are redesigns, not more N.
recommended_next.narrative: Combined with the ablation (traces suggestive, ~2.5x strong-program rate) and this null on skill transfer, the emerging picture: the repair loop's power lives in per-run trace-guided repair, not (yet demonstrably) in cross-task skill accumulation.
